headline: The $280K counter went out and the seller acknowledged it — Monday's real clock is 10:30 AM, when the buyer's agent brings an HVAC contractor to your Lake Crest seller's house on a repair request nobody has seen yet.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 THE COUNTER WENT OUT AND THE DEAL IS ALIVE — this board's midday read was wrong and is corrected. Receipts in order: the counter recommendation and net sheet were SENT to seller Seth B. at 9:50 AM; he answered 11:43 “On a boat in gulf. I call when we get on road”; Cassie C. (RE/MAX Advantage) chased by email at 3:01 PM — “Just checking back in. Any news?”; and at 3:17 PM Gene texted Seth “counter sent” and got 👍🏻 back a minute later. The 7:00 PM void passed with the ball in the BUYERS' court, not with the offer walking. ⚠️ Unverified and not to be asserted: no counter document to her exists in Gmail, and the file has carried both $292,000 and $301,000 — which number went is unknown.
hotSignals.action: Monday, in order. First call Cassie C. — she asked for news at 3:01 and, as far as Gmail shows, never got a written reply; get her buyers' response to the counter. Then call Seth with whatever comes back; he's off the boat now. ⚠️ Do not quote a counter figure to anyone until it's confirmed which one went out. Their pre-approval is written to exactly $280,000 — if the counter landed above that, their lender has to re-paper it, which takes a day or two, so do not read Monday silence as a no. The one genuinely open question since 7/16 is unchanged: is the ARC Realty offer alive? If it is, your seller is CHOOSING between two offers rather than waiting on one.

hotSignals.signal: 🔴 AN HVAC CONTRACTOR IS BEING BROUGHT TO THE HOUSE AT 10:30 TOMORROW. Booked at 3:18 PM today by buyer's agent Manda L. (ARC Realty Vestavia) as the SECOND inspection on this file, and the showing remark reads verbatim: “Meeting hvac company.” Friday's repair request has still never arrived, so this is the first hard signal of what the buyers are actually chasing — ten days before the 8/14 close. ⚠️ NOT ASSERTED: that anything is wrong with the HVAC, what a contractor will find, or that this threatens the close. The receipt says an HVAC company is being met, nothing more.
hotSignals.action: Call your seller before 10:30 so he isn't surprised by strangers at his house — and do NOT open by announcing a problem you can't name. Same call, get the thing that has been asked five times: a weekday DATE the sellers meet City of Hoover, not “next week.” Then call Manda L. with that date — she texted on a Saturday citing a clock, and a real date is what turns worry into a timeline. Don't re-litigate whether the buyers should be concerned; give them the date. Then the free move nobody has made: the written “interested: Yes” backup buyer, Kulsum B. (Keller Williams Hoover), is seven days uncalled — and she is the same agent booked on Ridge Trail, so one call does both.

hotSignals.signal: 🟡 THE CANCELLATION HAS A REASON, AND THE REASON IS REBOOKABLE. Quin W. of EXIT Realty Southern Select booked showing #11 on Saturday afternoon and cancelled at 11:44 this morning — the stated reason on the notice is that the buyer got called into work. That is a scheduling problem, not a lost buyer, and it means the third distinct buyer in eight days is still live.
hotSignals.action: Rebook it with Quin W. first — then you call your seller with a date in hand instead of an apology. He occupies this house and has heard nothing from you in seven days, and the conditional re-offer passed the 96-hour mark at 12:16 today with the same answer as the 48- and 72-hour marks. Keep the real lever in view when you talk: the re-offering buyers' own home is STILL not under contract and goes live tomorrow.
